newsitem.title: ITALY: Two dead, 17 injured in Italian railway accident.
newsitem.headline: Two dead, 17 injured in Italian railway accident.

text.p: Two people were killed and 17 injured on Monday when a single locomotive collided with a passenger train in northern Italy, civil protection officials said.
The two trains, run by the private Ferrovie Nord Milano company, collided head-on in late morning on the Brescia-Edolo line northeast of Milan.
Civil protection officials confirmed that a conductor and an engine driver were killed and 17 passengers injured. Fire officials had earlier put the death toll at four.
All the injured were being treated at nearby hospitals and three were in a serious condition, the officials said.
The accident occurred on a curved section of track near a level crossing in open country between two stations about 100 km (60 miles) from Milan.
A railway spokesman said the train coming from Brescia was a single locomotive while the other had two packed passenger carriages.
Road conditions are atrocious in many parts of Italy which has been paralysed by cold weather and heavy snowfalls.
Italian television said the cause of the crash was not yet known but frozen points was mentioned as a possible factor.
